facts.statement: Lucasuchus is an extinct genus belonging to the group of armored reptiles known as aetosaurs.
facts.quote: Lucasuchus is an extinct genus of aetosaur.

facts.statement: Lucasuchus possessed elongated horns on its lateral osteoderms, a feature shared with other members of the subfamily Desmatosuchinae.
facts.quote: The presence of elongate lateral osteoderm horns is shared by all of these genera, which make up the subfamily Desmatosuchinae.

facts.statement: The genus Lucasuchus was named in 1995 in honor of the American paleontologist Spencer G. Lucas.
facts.quote: The genus was named in 1995 after the American paleontologist Spencer G. Lucas.

facts.statement: Fossils of Lucasuchus have been discovered in the Bull Canyon Formation of the Dockum Group in Quay County, New Mexico.
facts.quote: Fossils have been found from the Bull Canyon Formation of the Dockum Group outcropping in the Revuelto Creek locality in Quay County, New Mexico.

facts.statement: All known specimens of Lucasuchus date to the Norian stage of the Late Triassic.
facts.quote: All specimens date back to the Norian stage of the Late Triassic.

facts.statement: Researchers have debated whether Lucasuchus represents a sexual dimorph of Longosuchus meadei or an ontogenetic stage of that species.
facts.quote: It has been suggested that Lucasuchus is either a sexual dimorph belonging to the same species as Longosuchus meadei or an ontogenetic stage of the species (meaning that it represents one particular age group).

facts.statement: Despite the debate, several characteristics suggest that Lucasuchus is a distinct species rather than a morphological variation of Longosuchus meadei.
facts.quote: However, several characteristics of Lucasuchus may indicate that it is indeed distinct from L. meadei rather than an example of morphological variation.

facts.statement: The paramedian osteoderms of Lucasuchus feature large conical projections, whereas Longosuchus has only low pyramidal bosses.
facts.quote: In Lucasuchus, the paramedians have large conical eminences, or projections, while in Longosuchus these projections are only present in the form of low pyramidal bosses.

facts.statement: Unlike Longosuchus, Lucasuchus lacks notches on the spikes of its lateral osteoderms.
facts.quote: Lucasuchus also lacks the emarginations (or notches) on the spikes of the lateral osteoderms that are seen in Longosuchus.

facts.statement: Lucasuchus is classified within the family Stagonolepididae.
Lucasuchus belongs to the subfamily Desmatosuchinae.
The type species of the genus Lucasuchus is Lucasuchus hunti.
The time range for Lucasuchus is estimated to be between 237 and 227.3 million years ago during the Carnian age.
facts.quote: Time range: Carnian to Carnian (237 to 227.3 million years ago)

rejected.statement: Recent studies suggest that Lucasuchus is distinct from other aetosaur genera and is likely more closely related to Desmatosuchus and Acaenasuchus than to Longosuchus.
rejected.quote: However, more recent studies concluded that Lucasuchus is not congeneric with any other known aetosaur genus, and is likely to be more closely related to Desmatosuchus and Acaenasuchus than to Longosuchus.

rejected.statement: Lucasuchus is distinguished from Longosuchus by having a clear radial pattern of pits and grooves on its paramedian osteoderms.
rejected.quote: For example, Lucasuchus has a clear radial pattern of pits and grooves on the paramedian osteoderms of the back while Longosuchus has only a random pattern of pits on the paramedians.
